column1: Shared memory (one memory connecting the four intelligences)
column2: 'Perfect meeting memory' (Granola Chat H2); 'Notes, actions and memory.' (hero) (https://www.granola.ai/)
column3: 'Everything shared becomes context your whole team can search'; 'Your team's context from calendar, email, past meetings, and CRM' (https://www.read.ai/)
column4: 'Customer Memory is an LLM-optimized ontology built from automatically permissioned ingestion of your team’s email, calendar, meetings, and Slack.'; 'Every agent, on every team, reads and writes the same multiplayer context graph.' (https://day.ai/)
column5: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all three use memory language on the homepage. Difference: Granola frames memory as personal recall of meetings (team sharing and an MCP "shared memory for your agents and your team" appear on other pages); Read AI frames it as team-searchable context from calendar, email, meetings and CRM; Day AI makes memory the product itself ("Customer Memory" context graph shared by every agent and person). Opportunity (testable hypothesis): Day AI is the closest counterexample in the whole set to a one-memory thesis; what may stay unclaimed is memory that also connects practice and coaching readiness, which none of the three mention, but test against Day AI's coaching-agent templates first. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built today: Layer 1 call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library). In build: memory layers two and three; email and Slack sources are In build or Planned. 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)' is flagged by the Narrative, so the cross-layer memory story is not a public claim yet.

column1: Cross-channel intelligence (calls, CRM, emails, Slack, documents)
column2: 'Works with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams and every other meeting app.' (hero bullets); 'Zoom, Meet, Teams, Huddles, in-person, on-the-go: capture conversations wherever you have them.' (https://www.granola.ai/)
column3: 'Works across all meeting platforms, emails, and messages.'; 'Read AI is independent and platform-agnostic—connecting across all your tools to deliver truly unified insights.' (https://www.read.ai/)
column4: Hero diagram text: Slack, Gong, Gmail, API, Snowflake feeding /company-brain; 'automatically permissioned ingestion of your team’s email, calendar, meetings, and Slack' (https://day.ai/)
column5: Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief delivered to Slack; documents via the Content Library. In build: reading email for deal context (Gmail, Outlook); summaries by email and Teams; meeting bot. Planned: CRM connection (Salesforce, HubSpot) and updates; reading deal conversations in Slack; deal status from email and Slack. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'; 'Everything about email and Slack tracking'.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all three claim multi-source capture. Difference: Granola's homepage is meeting-centric (every meeting app plus in-person), with CRM and Slack on integration pages; Read AI spans meetings, email and messages and stresses platform independence; Day AI ingests email, calendar, meetings and Slack and also pulls from Gong and Snowflake. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): channel breadth is table stakes here; note that Granola is also a Built transcript source for PitchSense, so Granola is both a competitor and an input. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; Slack delivery of summaries and pre-call briefs; documents via the Content Library. Email reading, Teams/email summaries and the meeting bot are In build; CRM connection and Slack deal reading are Planned. Public copy can name calls and documents only.

(https://www.granola.ai/); CRO page: 'And when you need to know why deals are stalling this quarter, you ask Granola.' (https://www.granola.ai/use-cases/sales)
column3: Not observed on the homepage (https://www.read.ai/); CRO page: 'Spot risks, surface insights, and push qualified deals forward — all with reasoning-based AI.' (https://www.read.ai/integrations/hubspot)
column4: 'keeps sam's pipeline honest: flags stalls, preps meetings, drafts replies'; agent skills 'deal risk flag' and 'stale deal nudge' (https://day.ai/)
column5: In build: deal and account pages with connected call history; deal risks (Watch / At risk); commitments tracking. Planned: agent answers about calls, deals and accounts; CRM connection. No forecasting capability at any status. Built today: list of every call, call summaries, Home, accounts and contacts created automatically.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all three reach deal visibility, but only Day AI shows it on the homepage (pipeline-analyst agent flagging stalls and risk). Difference: Granola answers deal questions from conversation history when asked; Read AI puts deal-risk detection in CRM Copilot on its CRM pages; Day AI replaces the CRM record itself with agent-maintained pipeline. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): deal visibility tied to call evidence is contested by Read AI and Day AI; check Read AI's help-center CRM Copilot documentation before positioning against it. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Deal and account pages, deal risks (Watch / At risk) and commitments tracking are In build; agent answers about deals and CRM connection are Planned; there is no forecasting capability at any status. Built today: the call list, call summaries, Home, and auto-created accounts and contacts. 'Know every deal' stays out of public copy.

column5: Built: Content Library with AI search and sources ('One home for approved content'); practice built from your own documents. Flagged: 'The security doc suggested from the Content Library'; 'Everything about creating one-pagers, decks and proposals'.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: none of the three makes a sales-content claim on the homepage. Difference: Day AI's only content signal is a customer testimonial about building a knowledge base from demo recordings (vendor claim) and a "knowledge" folder in its diagram; Granola and Read AI generate documents from meetings (follow-ups, briefs) but show no content library. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): approved sales content tied to calls looks unclaimed by this group on the inspected pages; test against Read AI's Ask Read document search before relying on it. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built: Content Library with AI search and sources; practice built from your own documents. Planned: content suggested per call and follow-up; sales content creation. The Narrative lists no approval or compliance workflow, and flags 'The security doc suggested from the Content Library' and 'Everything about creating one-pagers, decks and proposals'.

column3: Not observed on the homepage (footer link 'Speaker Coach' only) (https://www.read.ai/)
column4: Not observed on the homepage (https://day.ai/); CRO page: 'One skill. Eighteen agents. Every call coached.' (https://day.ai/use-cases)
column5: Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays); tracks; skills and scoring set by Enablement; scores with evidence on every practice session; readiness per rep and scenario; coaching suggestions for managers; one-click drills with before-and-after results. In build: pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls on your skills. Flagged: 'Checks the score on the next real call'.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all three frame coaching as feedback on real calls, not practice. Difference: Granola points managers at call evidence (and its own blog says "Granola doesn't have a native coach"); Read AI's Speaker Coach scores clarity, inclusion and impact and states it "eliminates the requirement of practice"; Day AI deploys a coaching skill to every rep's agent. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): roleplay and practice remain unclaimed by all three on the inspected pages; the angle to test is practice linked to the same memory these vendors use for call review. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays), tracks, Enablement-set skills and scoring, scores with evidence, readiness per rep and scenario, manager coaching suggestions, one-click drills. In build: the pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls. 'Checks the score on the next real call' is flagged, so the call-tied angle is a proposal item with a date, not public copy.

column5: Built: summaries delivered to Slack; pre-call brief in Slack 30 minutes before each meeting; accounts and contacts created automatically; Home list of what needs each rep today. In build: follow-up email drafts; agent proposals that a person approves. Planned: CRM updates; sending approved follow-up emails. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'.
column6: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: all three lead with admin relief (notes, follow-ups, action routing, CRM entry). Difference: Granola and Read AI automate post-meeting output for a person; Day AI assigns the work to named agents that run on schedules and events, with approval. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): admin reduction is crowded in this group and is not a differentiator for PitchSense. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): Built admin reduction is limited to Slack summaries, pre-call briefs in Slack, auto-created accounts and contacts, and the Home list. Follow-up email drafts and agent proposals are In build; CRM updates and sending approved follow-ups are Planned. 'The CRM use cases' are flagged, so admin reduction cannot be a lead claim.
